en: Two is someone with no sales experience, but has deep product experience or an engineer and can think about things in a unique way where the market is like, "Oh, this is so interesting."
zh: 第二种是没有任何销售经验，但有深厚产品经验的人，或者是工程师，能以独特的方式思考问题，市场会觉得，“哦，这太有趣了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Taking a typical salesperson then and putting them into a sales role almost always is where people get frustrated.
zh: 然后找一个典型的销售人员并把她们放入销售角色，几乎总是人们感到沮丧的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: The market, it feels salesy.
zh: 市场会觉得这很有推销味。

speaker: Unknown
en: The market doesn't want to be sold to, they want to buy.
zh: 市场不想被推销给，他们想买。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know that it's very hard to hire a really good enterprise salesperson.
zh: 而且我知道雇佣一个非常优秀的企业级销售人员是非常难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number of people that I've interviewed, I can count on my hand the ones that I get really, really excited by.
zh: 我面试过的人数，我能用手数得过来那些让我真正、真正兴奋的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost like coming across a great founder.
zh: 这简直就像遇到了一个伟大的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not as common as everyone expects, and I think that that's true for engineering.
zh: 这并不像大家预期的那样常见，我认为这对工程领域也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that that's true for sales and I think a lot of people, sales is like, "Oh, just throw a body into it.
zh: 我认为这对销售也是如此，我认为很多人，销售就是，“噢，随便往里面扔个人就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product will do the work."
zh: 产品会干活。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Advice I often hear is don't hire a senior VP of salesperson from a bigger company.
zh: 我经常听到的建议是，不要从大公司雇佣高级销售副总裁或销售人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree with that?
zh: 你同意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's like to senior?
zh: 什么是资深到什么程度？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so the bigger company thing, the brand was doing all of the work.
zh: 是的，所以大公司那点事儿，品牌在那做了所有的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The brand built the trust.
zh: 品牌建立了信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need this person to be able to build the trust and they're usually, the product is still so new.
zh: 你需要这个人能够建立信任，而且通常来说，产品还很新。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product is the founder in the zero to one stage.
zh: 在 0 到 1 阶段，产品就是创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product is just starting to get a case study.
zh: 产品才刚刚开始有一个案例研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: You probably have maybe a few references, but it's still very, very early days.
zh: 你可能也许有几个参考，但仍然是非常、非常早期的日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need the market to believe the salesperson and you need that market to know that they're trustworthy.
zh: 你需要市场相信这个销售人员，你需要那个市场知道他们是值得信赖的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A VP of sales at a large company, I would say, they're best suited for a large company because one to 10, you're running through walls.
zh: 大公司的销售副总裁，我想说，他们最适合大公司，因为在 1 到 10 阶段，你要拼命。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to figure out, you're doing a lot of convincing, you're doing a lot of educating, you're doing a lot of creative deal crafting.
zh: 你必须弄清楚，你在做大量的说服工作，你在做大量的教育工作，你在做大量创造性的交易设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of owning the frame.
zh: 还要拥有大量的框架主导权。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not necessarily selling a product, it's selling that future value, which a VP of sales at a large companies, it's very different.
zh: 这不一定是在卖产品，这是在推销未来的价值，这对于大公司的销售副总裁来说，是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a different game.
zh: 这是不同的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of like the SMB and enterprise.
zh: 这有点像 SMB 和企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting you said when you described the profile of a great hire here is you said they don't need to have done sales.
zh: 你说这很有趣，当你描述这里优秀候选人的特征时，你说他们不需要有销售经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they have done sales, what's a number years or kind of what do you look for that tells you, "Okay, this is a good fit for the first hire."
zh: 如果他们有销售经验，你要看多少年或者你主要看重什么来告诉你，“好的，这很适合作为第一位候选人。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually think it's less about experience and more about the person.
zh: 我实际上认为这更多是关于人而不是经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does this person make you feel good?
zh: 这个人让你感觉良好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to buy from this person?
zh: 你想向这个人购买吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Jason, Jason Lemkin said that best.
zh: 我想 Jason，Jason Lemkin 说得最好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you want to buy from this person?
zh: 你想从这个人那里买东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can they sell you a pen?
zh: 他们能把一支笔卖给你吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The classic.
zh: 经典问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，确实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they mimic or mirror the market they're selling to?
zh: 他们会模仿或镜像他们销售的市场吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's much easier to buy from someone that looks and feels like you than it does from somebody that's in a totally different realm.
zh: 从一个看起来和感觉都像你那里购买比从一个完全不同领域的人那里购买要容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, an executive wants to talk to another senior person.
zh: 而且，一位高管想和另一位资深人士交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't want to talk to someone that just graduated from college and is selling them the new way of working.
zh: 他们不想和一个刚大学毕业的人交谈并向他们推销新的工作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they know?
zh: 他们懂什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's tricky.
zh: 所以我觉得这很棘手。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say someone with no sales experience makes it feel different and special, that's what I like about it.
zh: 我会说一个没有销售经验的人会让人觉得与众不同和特别，这就是我喜欢它的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone with sales experience knows how to navigate and probably be qualified better, but it's almost like the blend of those two things.
zh: 有销售经验的人知道如何导航并且可能更合格，但这几乎是这两者的结合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why I go back to cosplaying the founder, which is like, could this person close a future employee?
zh: 这就是我为什么要回到“扮演创始人”这一点，就像，这个人能搞定一位未来的员工吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they get excited about the problems they're solving internally and the vision that they get to sell to?
zh: 他们对他们正在解决的内部问题和他们要推销的愿景感到兴奋吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This actually was a reader question, listener question from Twitter.
zh: 这实际上是一个读者问题，来自 Twitter 的听众提问。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Peter Dedenne asked, "How do you make this first salesperson as enthusiastic about the product as you?
zh: 所以 Peter Dedenne 问道，“你如何让这位第一位销售人员像你一样对产品充满热情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something you could do?
zh: 有什么你能做的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it more just they already are and you just leverage that?"
zh: 还是说更多是他们本来就是这样而你只是利用这一点？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Incentives.
zh: 激励。

en: Salespeople love to make money.
zh: 销售人员喜欢赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Easy.
zh: 简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if they know it's possible, if they know it's possible, you'll be shocked what people can get done.
zh: 所以如果他们知道这是可能的，如果他们知道这是可能的，你会惊讶于人们能完成什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they see how much they could make.
zh: 如果他们看到他们能赚多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 神奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine there still also has to be an innate excitement about the product and the opportunity.
zh: 我想仍然必须有一种对产品和机会的内在兴奋感。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 他们必须相信它。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to believe in the founder, but incentives usually make the world go round, but yeah, is this person, are they asking the right questions to the founder?
zh: 他们必须相信创始人，但激励通常让世界运转，但是是的，这个人，他们在向创始人问正确的问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The best thing to do is have the founder join the first five calls.
zh: 最好的办法是让创始人加入前五个电话。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 五个电话后你就知道这个人是否有能力，不要害怕解雇。

speaker: Unknown
en: One in every two salespeople usually are fired.
zh: 每两个销售人员中通常有一个会被解雇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's a very high failure rate.
zh: 是的，这是一个非常高的失败率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you can tell pretty quickly how it's going.
zh: 因为你可以很快地看出事情会如何发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can tell, or the vision of the founders is just very wrong.
zh: 你可以看出来，或者创始人的愿景只是非常错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of incentives, do you have any quick advice on how to structure their comp?
zh: 说到激励，关于如何构建他们的薪酬结构你有什么快速建议吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like how much they earn?
zh: 就像他们赚多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's usually 50/50.
zh: 通常是五五开。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's 50% OTE.
zh: 所以是 50% OTE。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's 50% base salary, 50% OTE.
zh: 所以是 50% 基本工资，50% OTE。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then how much of the sale do they typically get?
zh: 然后他们通常能拿到销售的多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: Say the first sales hire.
zh: 比如说第一位销售人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: It depends on the size of the deal, but in technology, it could be anywhere between eight and 12%.
zh: 这取决于交易规模，但在科技行业，可能在 8% 到 12% 之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So rounds out around 10%.
zh: 所以大约在 10% 左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: When do you hire the first salesperson?
zh: 你什么时候招聘第一位销售人员？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it around the 1 million ARR mark usually?
zh: 通常是在 100 万 ARR 这个阶段吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's around that 1 million ARR, mark and I, and it's usually when you have your first seven to 10 customers and there's some pattern recognition around it that you can share with somebody else, there's some consistencies.
zh: 是的，是在那个 100 万 ARR 阶段，而且我，而且通常是在你有了前 7 到 10 个客户时，并且周围有一些模式识别，你可以与另一个人分享，有一些一致性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, it's just like that would be very hard.
zh: 否则，那就只是那样会非常困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically as a founder, you have to figure out how to sell enough times so that you can show someone, "Here's what's working."
zh: 基本上作为创始人，你必须弄清楚如何销售足够多次，这样你就可以向某人展示，“这就是行之有效的方法。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the common thing I hear, "Well, I'm a $10 million business.
zh: 这是我常听到的一件事，“嗯，我是个 1000 万美元的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm in this small business space.
zh: 我处于这个小业务领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're $0 in enterprise."
zh: 你在企业领域是 0。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a zero to one right now in enterprise.
zh: 现在在企业领域是从 0 到 1。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a totally different game.
zh: 这是一个完全不同的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a different value proposition, it's a different deal structuring, it's a different target market.
zh: 这是一个不同的价值主张，这是一个不同的交易结构，这是一个不同的目标市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a different risk tolerance.
zh: 这是一个不同的风险容忍度。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's totally different.
zh: 完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So don't be blindsided when-
zh: 所以不要被蒙在鼓里当——

speaker: Lenny
en: It doesn't work.
zh: 它不起作用。

zh: ……当你进入一个新市场时，有很多东西需要「忘却」。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the advice here is make yourself sell up until around a million ARR, especially if you're trying to go enterprise selling to enterprises yourself as a founder, which is really hard.
zh: 所以这里的建议是让你自己卖到大约 100 万 ARR，特别是如果你试图进入企业领域，作为创始人自己向企业销售，这真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have so much to do and you have to be selling this thing for a long time time.
zh: 你有太多事情要做，而且你必须长时间销售这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then try and find someone that you get excited by.
zh: 然后试着找一个让你感到兴奋的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's funny, if you ask the founder, are you excited by your salesperson?
zh: 有趣的是，如果你问创始人，你为你的销售人员感到兴奋吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what the real answer is.
zh: 我很好奇真正的答案是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, "Well, it's a button to see it in.
zh: 就像是，“嗯，那是个按钮把它搞定。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It was hard to hire, so."
zh: 当时很难招聘，所以。”

speaker: Lenny
en: Interesting. I remember, I think it was Jason's advice was to hire two people immediately.
zh: 有趣。我记得，我想那是 Jason 的建议是立即招聘两个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can compare them.
zh: 这样你可以比较他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree with that?
zh: 你同意这一点吗？

speaker: Unknown
zh: 百分之百同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, because of the 50% failure rate.
zh: 是的，因为 50% 的失败率。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's exactly right.
zh: 我认为那完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, even a tall order, go find two people that are good.
zh: 所以是的，即使是个艰巨的任务，去找两个优秀的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think that that's right because one in two will fail.
zh: 但是的，我认为那是对的，因为两个中有一个会失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, let me ask you another reader question from Hang Huang.
zh: 好的，让我问你另一个来自 Hang Huang 的读者问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is kind of in a different direction.
zh: 这有点不同的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he says, "The biggest challenge is always cutting through the noise to get that initial meeting with the right decision maker.
zh: 所以他说，“最大的挑战总是要穿过噪音，获得与正确决策者的初次会面。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you even get their attention?"
zh: 你甚至如何获得他们的关注？”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the vision.
zh: 是愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the opportunity that you're selling?
zh: 你在推销什么机会？

speaker: Unknown
en: That if they are excited by that, they will take a call.
zh: 如果他们对此感到兴奋，他们就会接听电话。

en: I see it all the time, and don't give away the farm.
zh: 我一直看到这种情况，不要把所有底牌都亮出来。

en: Keep it to three sentences.
zh: 把它保持在三句话。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我知道我在我们第一次通话时说过这个，但说一些反直觉的话，他们可能会感觉不同。

en: Make it feel like they can learn from you by taking a 15-minute call.
zh: 让他们觉得通过 15 分钟的通话可以从你那里学到东西。

zh: 你看到那些标准，比如，“哦，我在你的 LinkedIn 上看到过你。”

zh: 还有，“你有没有希望通过 15% 增长你的业务？”

zh: 健康的 inbound 通常是由市场主导的倡议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's a marketing game.
zh: 所以那是一场市场营销的游戏。

zh: 这取决于你在卖什么样的交易价值。

zh: 你是在卖一笔 5,000 美元的交易吗？

zh: 它必须由市场主导才能让这个引擎运转起来。

zh: 如果你是在卖一笔 100,000 美元的交易，你在第一天就要做 outbound。

zh: 所以再次强调，它把它分成了那些类别。

en: This is like that blending of the, I see a blending of that question.

en: This is where you're doing small business marketing-led activities or are you a sales-led organization selling a $100,000 deal?

en: Oh this awesome.

en: ... Through so much.

speaker: Unknown
en: This is exactly what I was hoping to get through and we've gone through so much advice that I think is going to be so helpful to so many people.
zh: 这正是我所希望能涵盖到的，我们已经讨论了很多建议，我认为这会对很多人非常有帮助。

zh: 其中之一是你经常问创始人一个问题，能打开他们的思维。
